expectationBasis: Users view available workbooks on the workbook home page. Each record displays "Last updated: <last updated value>" and provides a link whose accessible name is the workbook name.

After the user clicks the link, the editor displays the same "Last updated: <last updated value>", the corresponding workbook name, worksheet tabs and order, current active worksheet, row and column structure, grid values, formula bar content, filter views, validation entry points, and pivot table results; data from another workbook must not appear in the current grid.
The evaluation seed contains the seeded workbook `Q3 Sales`, worksheet `Sheet1`, and cell A1 value `Region`.

The current editor page entry in the browser must be directly accessible and continue to identify the same workbook after refresh; visiting that exact workbook state in the same or a later browser session must restore the workbook’s most recent successful state without requiring navigation through the home page.

After the user refreshes the page or reopens the visible destination from the application entry point, the successful result and workbook `Q3 Sales`, worksheet `Sheet1`, cell `A1=Region` remain persisted; on failure, the original seeded state remains unchanged.
successful workbook modifications must remain available through that visible workbook state.

uncoveredOutcomes.reason: REQ-1-1-1 declares only viewing and opening an existing seeded workbook; no named input control and no validation or permission rule is stated for this flow, so no failure beside a named control can be triggered or asserted.
Opening the already seeded workbook creates no new record, and REQ-1-1-1 declares no partial-record path for the view/open flow, so no partial-record result can be observed.

No failure trigger is defined for the view/open flow, so the plan cannot provoke a failure and then assert that the original seeded state is unchanged; the persistence result that is expressible is asserted in the refresh case.
